subtitle: A nursemaid between a dying kingdom and a living child

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle interior wide of a dim Rajput palace chamber at night
panels.action: Panna Dai kneels between two cradles in a shadowed stone chamber, one hand on a sleeping royal child, the other reaching toward a small bundle that suggests her own son, as distant torches and looming swords flicker at the doorway.

dialogue.text: In the night after Chittor’s fall, tradition remembers Panna Dai facing an unthinkable choice: her son, or the bloodline of Mewar.

i18n.hi: चित्तौड़ की गिरावट की रात, परंपरा पन्ना दाई को उस घड़ी पर याद करती है: अपना बेटा, या मेवाड़ की नस्ल।

panels.shot: high, mournful aerial wide over the ruined fort of Chittor
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of the scarred ramparts of Chittor, towers blackened, courtyards empty, with smoke hanging low over the stone city and the vast plain of Mewar stretching beyond.

dialogue.text: In 1535, Bahadur Shah of Gujarat stormed Chittor. The old capital of Mewar stood blackened, its defenders dead, its women gone to jauhar, its future uncertain.

i18n.hi: १५३५ में, गुजरात के बहादुर शाह ने चित्तौड़ लूट लिया। मेवाड़ की पुरानी राजधानी जली‑काली, रक्षक मरे, औरतें जौहर कर चुकीं, आगे क्या होगा कोई नहीं जानता था।

panels.shot: medium interior wide of a royal hall, emptied and echoing
panels.action: An abandoned audience hall in Chittor with toppled spears and a vacant throne, faint dust drifting through shafts of light from high jali windows.

dialogue.text: Rana Vikramaditya, brother of the slain Rana Ratan Singh II, held a shaken court. The Gujarati threat had passed, but inside Mewar, pride, insult and resentment were gathering.

i18n.hi: मरे हुए राणा रतनसिंह द्वितीय के भाई, राणा विक्रमादित्य, डगमगाती दरबार संभाले बैठे थे। गुजराती खतरा हट चुका था, पर मेवाड़ के भीतर घमंड, अपमान और रंजिशें उबल रही थीं।

panels.shot: tight three-quarter view on a young prince with attendants, in a small palace courtyard
panels.action: A small boy, Udai Singh, in simple royal clothes, plays quietly beside a low stone basin as veiled attendants watch, their faces tense despite the calm setting.

dialogue.text: Among the survivors was a child, Udai Singh, son of the late Rana Sanga. If he lived, the old Sisodia line would live through him. If he did not, others could claim the throne.

i18n.hi: बचे लोगों में एक बच्चा था – उदयसिंह, दिवंगत राणा सांगा का बेटा। वह जीता तो पुरानी सिसोदिया रगें उसी से चलतीं, वह मरता तो और दावेदार उग आते।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Panna Dai in a palace nursery
panels.action: Panna Dai stands in a sunlit nursery, one arm gently around young Udai Singh, the other cradling an unseen infant at her hip, her weathered face watchful yet tender.

dialogue.text: In the women’s quarters, one figure moved quietly at the centre of his world: Panna, called Panna Dai, the nursemaid. She fed him, taught him, watched the shadows lengthen on the walls.

i18n.hi: जनानखाने में उसके छोटे से जहांन के बीचोंबीच एक ही परछाईं थी – पन्ना, पन्ना दाई, उसकी धाय। वही खिलाती, वही सिखाती, वही दीवारों पर सरकती छायाएं देखती।

panels.shot: dramatic half-lit medium of Banvir conferring with armed followers
panels.action: In a darker hall, Banvir, a determined nobleman of mixed birth, leans forward over a low table toward armed Rajput retainers, his hand resting on the hilt of his sword, sconces casting sharp shadows.

dialogue.text: Sources speak of Banvir, a relative raised in Mewar’s service, who felt wronged by his standing and by Vikramaditya’s temper. From such hurts, plots and new hopes for the gaddi were born.

i18n.hi: कहानियां बाणवीर का जिक्र करती हैं – एक रिश्तेदार, जो मेवाड़ की सेवा में पलकर भी अपने दर्जे और विक्रमादित्य के गुस्से से कुढ़ा रहता था। ऐसे जख्मों से ही षड्यंत्र और गद्दी के नए सपने जन्मे।

panels.shot: dynamic interior wide of a sudden night attack inside the palace
panels.action: Armoured men surge through a palace corridor at night, bare swords catching torchlight as startled servants shrink against the carved stone walls.

dialogue.text: One night, the quiet finally cracked. Banvir’s men moved through the palace with drawn steel. In the darkness, Vikramaditya’s brief, troubled rule ended, and the path to the child prince lay open.

i18n.hi: एक रात, सन्नाटा आखिर टूट गया। बाणवीर के लोग नंगी तलवारें लिए महल में फैल गए। अंधेरे में विक्रमादित्य का छोटा, अशांत राज खत्म हुआ, और बाल‑राजकुमार तक का रास्ता खुल गया।

panels.shot: close-up on Panna Dai’s face in lamplight
panels.action: Panna Dai’s face is lit by a small oil lamp, eyes wide and alert, as she listens, the faint outline of two cradles behind her in the shadows.

dialogue.text: What followed in Panna’s chamber is told not by inscriptions, but by later bards like Muhnot Nainsi. Tradition says she heard the whispers, saw the fear in the servants’ eyes, and understood.

i18n.hi: पन्ना के कमरे में क्या हुआ, ये शिलालेख नहीं, बल्कि बाद के चारण, जैसे मुहणोत नैणसी, सुनाते हैं। परंपरा कहती है, उसने फुसफुसाहटें सुनीं, नौकरों की आंखों में डर देखा, और सब समझ गई।

panels.shot: medium interior of Panna between two sleeping children
panels.action: In the dim nursery, Panna Dai kneels between two low cots: on one lies young Udai Singh, on the other a smaller child; she reaches toward both with trembling hands, jaw clenched.

dialogue.text: The khyat says she looked at the two sleeping boys: the Rana’s son, and her own Chandan. Banvir, it is said, meant to kill the child who could rival his claim.

i18n.hi: ख्यात कहती है, उसने दो सोते बच्चों को देखा – राणा का बेटा और अपना चंदन। कहा जाता है, बाणवीर उस बालक को मारना चाहता था जो उसके दावे को चुनौती दे सके।

panels.shot: low-angle tight shot on Panna lifting Udai into a basket
panels.action: Panna Dai stoops quickly, lifting Udai Singh and setting him into a sturdy wicker basket lined with cloth, her face set in grim resolve as distant footsteps echo outside.

dialogue.text: In the tale, she makes her choice in a heartbeat. Udai into the grain basket, a cloth over him, a hurried prayer. The cradle that held her own child is left in its place.

i18n.hi: कहानी में वह धड़कन भर में फैसला कर लेती है। उदय को धान की टोकरी में, ऊपर कपड़ा, होठों पर दबी प्रार्थना। झूला, जिसमें उसका अपना बच्चा सोया था, वहीं छोड़ दिया जाता है।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder view of Banvir’s men entering as Panna kneels by a cot
panels.action: Seen from behind the silhouettes of armed men in the doorway, Panna Dai kneels beside a cot, her back straight, hands resting on its edge, as if watching a sleeping child.

dialogue.text: The Nainsi tradition says Banvir’s men burst into the nursery. They saw a child in royal cloth on the bed, and a silent nurse beside him. The steel that sought the prince never checked its aim.

i18n.hi: नैणसी की परंपरा कहती है, बाणवीर के लोग हड़कते हुए शिशुकक्ष में घुसे। बिस्तर पर शाही वस्त्रों में बच्चा दिखा, और पास एक चुप धाय। जो इस्पात राजकुमार को खोज रहा था, उसने अपनी वार नहीं रोकी।

panels.shot: tight profile of Panna, eyes closed, turned away from the cot
panels.action: A close side view of Panna Dai, eyes shut tightly, face turned away from the cot, her hands gripping the edge so hard her knuckles are pale, a shadow of a drawn sword beyond.

panels.shot: medium shot of Panna lifting the heavy basket, a dark corridor beyond
panels.action: Panna Dai hefts the covered basket with effort, holding it close, as she steps into a narrow stone passage lit only by a faint torch at the far end.

dialogue.text: So the story goes: when the men left, the nurse lifted the basket that held Udai Singh and walked into the darkness. Behind her, the cost of that walk lay on a simple cot.

i18n.hi: कहानी आगे कहती है – जब वे चले गए, धाय ने उदयसिंह वाला टोकरा उठाया और अंधेरे में चल पड़ी। उसके पीछे, उस एक कदम की कीमत एक साधारण खाट पर छूट गई।

panels.shot: wide shot of Panna slipping through a postern gate into the night
panels.action: Panna Dai, carrying the covered basket, slips out of a small postern gate in the fort wall into the open night, stars faint above and the hulking silhouette of Chittor looming behind.

dialogue.text: Later accounts picture her leaving Chittor by a quieter gate, hugging the fort’s shadows, cradling the basket that now held Mewar’s last direct heir. Banvir, they say, believed the child was dead.

i18n.hi: बाद की कहानियां उसे चित्तौड़ से एक सुनसान फाटक से निकलते, किले की दीवारों से सटकर चलते दिखाती हैं, टोकरी में अब मेवाड़ का आखिरी सीधा वारिस। कहते हैं, बाणवीर को यकीन था बच्चा मर चुका है।

panels.shot: wide landscape shot of rugged hills as Panna travels with the basket
panels.action: Against a backdrop of rugged Aravalli hills and thorn trees, Panna Dai walks along a narrow path, the basket balanced carefully, her sari dusty, sun low and harsh.

dialogue.text: The tradition follows her over stony hills and ravines, through village tracks and forest paths, until she reaches Kumbhalgarh, the hill fort where Udai Singh can be hidden and raised quietly.

i18n.hi: परंपरा उसके साथ कंकरीले पहाड़, गहरी खाइयां, गांवों के पगडंडी और जंगल की राहें पार करती है, जब तक वह कुम्भलगढ़ नहीं पहुंचती – वह पहाड़ी किला जहां उदयसिंह को छिपाकर पाला जा सके।

panels.shot: impressive wide shot of Kumbhalgarh fort on a ridge
panels.action: The massive walls of Kumbhalgarh wind along a high ridge, gates and bastions rising against the sky, small figures visible near a gate to show the fort’s scale and remoteness.

dialogue.text: Kumbhalgarh, Rana Kumbha’s hill fort, became in these stories a cradle. While Banvir ruled at Chittor, a child was said to be growing in the hills, watched by his nurse and a few loyal men.

i18n.hi: कुम्भलगढ़, राणा कुम्भा का पहाड़ी दुर्ग, इन कथाओं में झूला बन जाता है। जब तक बाणवीर चित्तौड़ पर राज करता है, कहा जाता है पहाड़ियों में एक बालक बढ़ रहा था – अपनी धाय और कुछ वफादारों की नजर में।

panels.shot: interior wide of a later court in Udaipur, men in council
panels.action: In a later, more orderly hall, Rajput nobles sit in council around a young Rana Udai Singh on a low throne, scrolls and spears beside them, their faces grave.

dialogue.text: Historically, we know this much for certain: Banvir’s rule did not last. The nobles of Mewar rallied around Udai Singh, removed the usurper, and in time the boy founded a new capital at Udaipur.

i18n.hi: इतिहास इतना तो साफ कहता है – बाणवीर का राज टिका नहीं। मेवाड़ के सरदार उदयसिंह के पीछे खड़े हुए, हड़पने वाले को हटा दिया, और आगे चलकर यही लड़का उदयपुर नाम की नई राजधानी बसाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of later bards reciting in a courtyard
panels.action: In a later century, a court bard stands in a palace courtyard, singing with raised hand as listeners sit around, one young boy leaning forward, eyes wide with wonder.

dialogue.text: By then, Panna’s name had entered song. Muhnot Nainsi and other chroniclers of Rajasthan wove her into Mewar’s memory, shaping a nursemaid into a symbol of duty carried beyond the measure of family.

i18n.hi: तब तक पन्ना का नाम गीतों में बस चुका था। मुहणोत नैणसी और राजस्थान के दूसरे इतिहासकारों ने उसे मेवाड़ की याद में पिरोया, एक धाय को परिवार से भी आगे जाती हुई फर्ज की प्रतीक बना दिया।

panels.shot: serene medium close-up of Panna Dai looking out over a valley from a rampart
panels.action: Panna Dai, in later years, stands on a quiet fort rampart, hands resting on the parapet, looking over a calm green valley, her face lined but steady, wind lifting the end of her sari.

dialogue.text: The records cannot prove every detail of her night, yet Mewar keeps her story. Between a throne and a cradle, Panna Dai shows how some choices leave no reward for the chooser, only a lineage that walks on.

i18n.hi: दस्तावेज उसकी उस रात के हर मोड़ को साबित नहीं कर पाते, पर मेवाड़ उसकी गाथा संभाले है। गद्दी और झूले के बीच, पन्ना दाई दिखाती है कि कुछ फैसलों में चुनने वाले के लिए कोई इनाम नहीं, बस एक नस्ल रहती है जो आगे चलती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: A nursemaid between a dying kingdom and a living child
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक धाय, एक मरता राज्य और एक जीवता बच्चा
